reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) reports high activation energies (~900–1000 kJ/mol) and reduced creep displacement for similar refractory HEAs (TaTiVWZr, HfTaTiVZr) and attributes them to severe lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion, but it does not test WTaTiVZr, does not measure toughness or crack-tip strain localization, and the temperature range studied (298–573 K) is narrower than the claimed 298–800 °C, leaving the link to enhanced toughness unsupported.
premises: Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits severe lattice distortion causing sluggish atomic diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion elevates the activation energy for dislocation motion across 298–800 °C.
Elevated activation energy retards creep deformation relative to pure tungsten.
Retarded creep reduces strain localization at crack tips, enhancing toughness and ductility.
